import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 6.9

by Yu. M. Gorchakov

Is the derived subgroup of any locally normal group decomposable into a product of at most
countable subgroups which commute elementwise?

Here a group is *locally normal* (in the sense of Kurosh) if every finite subset of it is
contained in a finite normal subgroup. A family of subgroups $(H_i)_{i \in I}$ *commutes
elementwise* if $xy = yx$ whenever $x \in H_i$, $y \in H_j$ and $i \neq j$; since such
subgroups normalise each other, their product is the subgroup they generate, that is, their
join $\bigsqcup_{i \in I} H_i$.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«6.9»

/-- A group $G$ is *locally normal* if every finite subset of $G$ is contained in a finite
normal subgroup of $G$. -/
def IsLocallyNormal (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ S : Finset G, ∃ N : Subgroup G, N.Normal ∧ Finite N ∧ (S : Set G) ⊆ N

/-- Every finite group is locally normal. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isLocallyNormal_of_finite (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite G] : IsLocallyNormal G :=
  fun _ => ⟨⊤, inferInstance, inferInstance, fun _ _ => Subgroup.mem_top _⟩

/--
Is the derived subgroup of any locally normal group decomposable into a product of at most
countable subgroups which commute elementwise?

That is, for every locally normal group $G$, is there a family $(H_i)_{i \in I}$ of at most
countable subgroups of $G$ with $xy = yx$ for all $x \in H_i$, $y \in H_j$, $i \neq j$, whose
join $\bigsqcup_{i \in I} H_i$ is the derived subgroup $[G, G]$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«6.9» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsLocallyNormal G →
      ∃ (ι : Type) (H : ι → Subgroup G),
        (∀ i, Countable (H i)) ∧
        (Pairwise fun i j => ∀ x ∈ H i, ∀ y ∈ H j, Commute x y) ∧
        ⨆ i, H i = commutator G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«6.9»
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The single-slot table and its notes (Kurosh-style locally normal, join as product, arbitrary index type, Countable including finite) match my reading of the statement.
modeling_decisions: 'Locally normal' is formalized in Kurosh's sense (every finite subset lies in a finite normal subgroup), as the decomposition table's notes prescribe; stated with Finset G, equivalent to the finite-Set or finitely-generated-subgroup formulations.

'Product' of the (possibly infinitely many) elementwise-commuting subgroups is taken as their join ⨆ i, H i (the subgroup they generate), which coincides with the set-theoretic product for finitely many mutually normalising subgroups; no direct-product (trivial intersection) requirement is imposed, matching the wording 'product' rather than 'direct product'.
Elementwise commutation is required only between distinct members of the family (Pairwise, i.e. i ≠ j); the individual subgroups H i are not required to be abelian.
'At most countable' is Countable ↥(H i), so finite subgroups are allowed.
The subgroups H i are subgroups of G; since their join equals commutator G they automatically lie in the derived subgroup.
The index type ι and the group G live in Type, following the convention of the other Kourovka files (e.g. 1_40.lean); this loses no generality for subgroups of a Type-level group.
Included a one-line @[category test] lemma (finite groups are locally normal) as the basic API test CONTRIBUTING.md asks for with bespoke definitions.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 6.9

by Yu. M. Gorchakov

Is the derived subgroup of any locally normal group decomposable into a product of
at most countable subgroups which commute elementwise?

Here a group is *locally normal* if every finite set of its elements is contained
in a finite normal subgroup.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«6.9»

/-- A group $G$ is *locally normal* if every finite set of elements of $G$ is contained
in a finite normal subgroup of $G$. -/
def IsLocallyNormal (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ S : Set G, S.Finite → ∃ N : Subgroup G, N.Normal ∧ Finite N ∧ S ⊆ N

/-- Every finite group is locally normal. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem IsLocallyNormal.of_finite (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite G] : IsLocallyNormal G :=
  fun _ _ => ⟨⊤, inferInstance, inferInstance, fun _ _ => Subgroup.mem_top _⟩

/-- Every locally normal group is a torsion group. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem IsLocallyNormal.isTorsion {G : Type*} [Group G] (hG : IsLocallyNormal G) :
    Monoid.IsTorsion G := by
  intro x
  obtain ⟨N, -, hN, hx⟩ := hG {x} (Set.finite_singleton x)
  have h : IsOfFinOrder (⟨x, hx rfl⟩ : N) := isOfFinOrder_of_finite _
  exact Submonoid.isOfFinOrder_coe.2 h

/--
Is the derived subgroup of any locally normal group decomposable into a product of
at most countable subgroups which commute elementwise?

That is, for every locally normal group $G$, is there a family $(H_i)_{i \in I}$ of
subgroups of $G$, each at most countable, such that $H_i$ and $H_j$ commute elementwise
for all $i \neq j$ and the derived subgroup $G' = [G, G]$ is the product of the $H_i$?
Since the $H_i$ commute elementwise, their product is the subgroup they generate, so
"$G'$ is the product of the $H_i$" is stated as $\bigsqcup_i H_i = G'$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«6.9» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsLocallyNormal G →
      ∃ (ι : Type) (H : ι → Subgroup G),
        (∀ i, Countable (H i)) ∧
        (∀ i j, i ≠ j → ∀ x ∈ H i, ∀ y ∈ H j, Commute x y) ∧
        ⨆ i, H i = commutator G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«6.9»

modeling_decisions: 'Locally normal' is formalized via finite subsets of G (∀ S finite, ∃ finite normal N ⊇ S), following the table's note; this is equivalent to the single-element version (every element lies in a finite normal subgroup) since a product of finitely many finite normal subgroups is a finite normal subgroup.

'Product of subgroups which commute elementwise' is rendered as the join ⨆ i, H i of a family indexed by an arbitrary type ι : Type (sufficient since G : Type, so any family of subgroups can be reindexed in Type). No directness (trivial intersections) is imposed, as the source says only 'product'.

Pairwise commutation is stated for indices i ≠ j (so repeated subgroups in the family would be forced to be abelian); this is equivalent to the set-based 'pairwise distinct subgroups commute' formulation after deduplication.
'At most countable' is `Countable (H i)` on the coerced subtype, which allows finite subgroups.
The subgroups H i are subgroups of G rather than of the derived subgroup; since their join equals commutator G, each H i ≤ commutator G automatically.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 6.9

by Yu. M. Gorchakov

Is the derived subgroup of any locally normal group decomposable into a product
of at most countable subgroups which commute elementwise?

Here a group is *locally normal* if every finite set of its elements is
contained in a finite normal subgroup (equivalently, every finitely generated
subgroup lies in a finite normal subgroup). Subgroups $H_i$ ($i \in I$) *commute
elementwise* if $xy = yx$ for all $x \in H_i$, $y \in H_j$ with $i \neq j$; the
family may be infinite, and the product of such a family is the subgroup
generated by them.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«6.9»

/-- A group $G$ is *locally normal* if every finite subset of $G$ is contained
in a finite normal subgroup of $G$. -/
def IsLocallyNormal (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ S : Finset G, ∃ N : Subgroup G, N.Normal ∧ Finite N ∧ ∀ x ∈ S, x ∈ N

/-- Every finite group is locally normal. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsLocallyNormal.of_finite (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite G] :
    IsLocallyNormal G :=
  fun _ => ⟨⊤, inferInstance, inferInstance, fun _ _ => Subgroup.mem_top _⟩

/-- Every subgroup of a locally normal group is locally normal. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsLocallyNormal.subgroup {G : Type*} [Group G] (hG : IsLocallyNormal G)
    (K : Subgroup G) : IsLocallyNormal K := by
  intro S
  obtain ⟨N, hN, hNfin, hS⟩ := hG (S.map ⟨Subtype.val, Subtype.val_injective⟩)
  refine ⟨N.comap K.subtype, hN.comap _, ?_, fun x hx => hS x (Finset.mem_map_of_mem _ hx)⟩
  exact Finite.of_injective (fun x : N.comap K.subtype => (⟨x.1.1, x.2⟩ : N)) fun x y h => by
    ext
    simpa using congrArg Subtype.val h

/--
Is the derived subgroup of any locally normal group decomposable into a product
of at most countable subgroups which commute elementwise?

That is, given a locally normal group $G$, is there a family of subgroups
$H_i$ ($i \in I$) of $G$, each at most countable, with $xy = yx$ for all
$x \in H_i$, $y \in H_j$, $i \neq j$, whose product is the derived subgroup
$G'$? Since the $H_i$ commute elementwise, each is normal in their product,
so the product $\prod_i H_i$ coincides with the join $\bigsqcup_i H_i$; it is
stated as $\bigsqcup_i H_i = G'$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«6.9» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsLocallyNormal G →
      ∃ (ι : Type) (H : ι → Subgroup G),
        (∀ i, Countable (H i)) ∧
        (∀ i j, i ≠ j → ∀ x ∈ H i, ∀ y ∈ H j, Commute x y) ∧
        ⨆ i, H i = commutator G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«6.9»

Formalized via Finset G rather than finitely generated subgroups; these are equivalent.

'Product of subgroups which commute elementwise' is formalized as the join ⨆ i, H i of an indexed family of subgroups of G with pairwise elementwise commutation for i ≠ j. Since pairwise elementwise-commuting subgroups are each normal in their join, the join equals the set of finite products, so this matches the product exactly; the family may be infinite (arbitrary ι : Type).

'At most countable' is `Countable ↥(H i)` (finite or countably infinite), so a countable derived subgroup trivially decomposes with a single factor — consistent with the source, which is only non-trivial for uncountable derived subgroups.

Requiring commutation only for i ≠ j (not for i = j) is deliberate: the factors need not be abelian. A non-injective family would force repeated factors to be abelian, but this does not change the existential since one may always pass to an injective family.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 6.9

by Yu. M. Gorchakov

Is the derived subgroup of any locally normal group decomposable into a product
of at most countable subgroups which commute elementwise?

Here a group is *locally normal* if every finite set of its elements is
contained in a finite normal subgroup (Kurosh, *The Theory of Groups*, §55).
Since the factors of the product are required to commute elementwise, the
product is the subgroup they generate, i.e. their join.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«6.9»

variable {G : Type*} [Group G]

/-- A group $G$ is *locally normal* if every finite subset of $G$ is contained in
a finite normal subgroup of $G$. -/
def IsLocallyNormal (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ s : Finset G, ∃ N : Subgroup G, N.Normal ∧ Finite N ∧ (s : Set G) ⊆ N

/-- Every finite group is locally normal. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isLocallyNormal_of_finite [Finite G] : IsLocallyNormal G :=
  fun _ => ⟨⊤, inferInstance, inferInstance, fun _ _ => Subgroup.mem_top _⟩

/--
Is the derived subgroup of any locally normal group decomposable into a product
of at most countable subgroups which commute elementwise?

That is, for every locally normal group $G$, is there a family $(H_i)_{i \in I}$
of at most countable subgroups of $G$ with $[H_i, H_j] = 1$ for all $i \neq j$
such that $G' = \prod_{i \in I} H_i$? Since the $H_i$ commute elementwise, their
product is the subgroup they generate, so this is stated as
$\bigsqcup_{i \in I} H_i = G'$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«6.9» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsLocallyNormal G →
      ∃ (ι : Type) (H : ι → Subgroup G),
        (∀ i, Countable (H i)) ∧
        (∀ i j, i ≠ j → ∀ x ∈ H i, ∀ y ∈ H j, Commute x y) ∧
        ⨆ i, H i = commutator G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«6.9»
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The table's reading (single yes/no question; locally normal = every finite subset lies in a finite normal subgroup; arbitrary index type; product = join of pairwise elementwise-commuting subgroups; at most countable = Countable, finite allowed) agrees with the notebook's statement and standard Russian-school terminology.
modeling_decisions: 'Locally normal' is read in the Kurosh/Kourovka sense: every finite subset of G is contained in a finite normal subgroup of G (equivalent to every finitely generated subgroup lying in a finite normal subgroup). This is not the same as 'locally finite' or 'FC-group' alone; it is their conjunction.

'Product' of the elementwise-commuting subgroups is formalized as the join ⨆ i, H i = commutator G. Since the factors commute elementwise, finite products of their elements already form a subgroup, so the join coincides with the set-theoretic product ∏ H_i; this is also what the decomposition table prescribes.

'At most countable subgroups' is read as each factor H i being at most countable (Countable (H i), finite allowed), not as the number of factors being countable; the index type ι is arbitrary (in Type). This matches the table and the Russian original ('не более чем счётных подгрупп').

'Commute elementwise' is required only for distinct indices (i ≠ j), as Commute x y for all x, y ∈ H i would force each factor to be abelian. A family with repeated entries can always be reindexed injectively, so this is equivalent to a Set (Subgroup G) formulation.
The factors H i are subgroups of G rather than of the derived subgroup; since ⨆ i, H i = commutator G forces each H i ≤ commutator G, this is equivalent.
G and ι are taken in Type (not Type*), following the convention of the other Kourovka files; ι : Type is not a restriction because any family can be reindexed by a set of subgroups of G.
The derived subgroup is Mathlib's commutator G = ⁅⊤, ⊤⁆.
